units.translation: The tragedians use either the simple αἰαῖ [alas!] sometimes within, sometimes outside the meter, or the doubled αἰαὶ αἰαῖ [alas! alas!], mostly placed outside the verse. About the spelling αἰαῖ (not αἰαί as in Apollonius in Bekker's Anecdota p. 556, 26 and in M by the first hand in Sophocles Oedipus Rex 754) it is established by the authority of Herodian in περὶ μόν. λέξ. [On Peculiar Words] p. 27, but the copyists in the manuscripts of the tragedians almost constantly divided it into αἶ αἶ (more rarely αἶ αἶ) and αἱ αἱ αἱ αἶ, sometimes writing αἶ three times, which no one used, or changing αἰαῖ into ἒ ἔ.
